This is the residual empty-case inconsistency — see §4.\n91\t\n92\t---\n93\t\n94\t## 3. Commands using custom `println!` serialization (Family B)\n95\t\n96\tTen commands serialize non-`Issue` data inline. This is largely **justified**: the `Formatter`\n97\ttrait is keyed to `&Issue`/`&[Issue]` and has no method for `Stats`, `VelocityStats`, `Event`,\n98\tbatch results, claim results, or dependency trees. They fall into three serialization styles:\n99\t\n100\t**`to_string_pretty(&T)` on a `Serialize` struct** (struct field order, 2-space indent):\n101\t- `stats` → `Stats` object (`:2589`)\n102\t- `velocity` → `Vec<VelocityStats>` array (`:2862`)\n103\t- `log` → `Vec<Event>` array via `crate::log::format_events_json()` (`src/log.rs:142-144`, called at `:3070`)\n104\t- `labels` → `Vec<String>` array (`:2495`)\n105\t- `mitosis` → `Vec<BatchResult>` array (`:2224`)\n106\t- `critical-path` → `CriticalPath` object with nested `beads[]` (`:3101`)\n107\t- `schema` → `Issue` object or `{\"schema\": SQL}` (`:2674`/`:2677`/`:2644`)\n108\t\n109\t**`serde_json::json!({...})` literal → `Display`/`to_string_pretty`** (keys **sorted\n110\talphabetically**, see §4):\n111\t- `claim` → single result object, hand-picked projection (`:1755`/`:1799`/`:1838`/`:1866`/`:1907`)\n112\t- `dep tree` → object with `nodes[]` (`:2398`/`:2408`)\n113\t- `schema` `\"all\"` target → `{\"schema\": SQL}` (`:2641`)\n114\t\n115\t**`to_string(&vec![out])` compact** (struct field order, single line):\n116\t- `show` → single-element array `[{…}]` (`:1464`) — array-wrapped for NEEDLE compatibility\n117\t\n118\t### `claim` detail (carried from bf-2x0p, still accurate)\n119\t\n120\t`claim` bypasses the formatter because it emits a **single** hand-picked projection mixing\n121\tfields from `ScoredBead`, `ClaimResult`, and the caller's `assignee`/`workspace` — not an\n122\t`Issue`, and not a struct's `Serialize`. Four mutually exclusive branches (dry-run / any /\n123\tfallback-any / normal) each emit a different object shape; every branch emits at least\n124\t`bead_id` + `assignee`, and every branch's empty/no-candidate case emits the literal `{}` via\n125\t`println!(\"{{}}\")` (`:1777`/`:1817`/`:1884`/`:1920`). Always a single object, never an array.\n126\t\n127\t---\n128\t\n129\t## 4. Inconsistencies in array / object formatting\n130\t\n131\tAfter `ready`'s migration, the old headline inconsistency (list/search JSONL vs. ready array)\n132\tis gone. What remains:\n133\t\n134\t1. **Container shape for \"list of beads\" is JSONL, but `show` is a 1-element array, and\n135\t   `ready`'s empty case is `[]`.**\n136\t   - `list`/`search`/`recent`/`ready`(non-empty) → JSONL (no array, no `[…]`)\n137\t   - `ready` (empty) → `[]`\n138\t   - `show` → always `[{…}]` (even though it is logically a single bead)\n139\t   - The remaining list-style commands that *do* use arrays (`velocity`, `log`, `mitosis`,\n140\t     `labels`) emit arrays of non-`Issue` rows, so the JSONL-vs-array split is now strictly\n141\t     \"Issue lists = JSONL, everything else = array.\" That is a defensible rule, but it is\n142\t     **undocumented** and breaks the reasonable expectation that `--format json` yields a\n143\t     parseable JSON document (JSONL is not a single JSON value).\n144\t\n145\t2. **Empty-case handling differs across list-style commands.**\n146\t   - `list`/`search`/`recent` → *no output at all* (empty string). A consumer reading stdout\n147\t     gets `EOF`/parse error, not `[]`.\n148\t   - `ready` → `[]`\n149\t   - `claim` → `{}` (single-object shape; appropriate)\n150\t   - `velocity`/`log`/`mitosis`/`labels` → `[]`\n151\t   - `stats`/`critical-path`/`dep tree` → always emit a full object (never truly \"empty\")\n152\t\n153\t3. **Compact vs. pretty printing.**\n154\t   - Compact (`to_string` / JSONL): `list`, `search`, `recent`, `ready`, `show`, `claim`\n155\t   - Pretty (`to_string_pretty`, 2-space indent): `stats`, `velocity`, `log`, `dep tree`,\n156\t     `labels`, `schema`, `mitosis`, `critical-path`\n157\t   - No command lets the user choose; it is hard-coded per command.\n158\t\n159\t4. **Trailing newline.**\n160\t   - Family A uses `print!` (the only newlines are the JSONL separators; no trailing newline\n161\t     after the last object).\n162\t   - Family B uses `println!` (trailing newline).\n163\t   - A consumer doing `bf search --format json | jq` is fine, but byte-for-byte stable\n164\t     consumers notice.\n165\t\n166\t5. **Key ordering.**\n167\t   - Struct-`Serialize` (`list`/`search`/`recent`/`ready`/`show`, `stats`, `velocity`, `log`,\n168\t     `labels`, `mitosis`, `critical-path`) → **struct declaration order**.\n169\t   - `json!` macro (`claim`, `dep tree`, `schema` `\"all\"`) → **alphabetical**. `serde_json`\n170\t     in `Cargo.toml` does **not** enable `preserve_order`, so `json!` builds a `BTreeMap`-backed\n171\t     `Map` and `Value::Display` sorts keys. (Empirically verified for `claim` in bf-2x0p.)\n172\t   - Harmless to generic-object parsers; differs byte-for-byte.\n173\t\n174\t---\n175\t\n176\t## 5. Notable defects / surprises\n177\t\n178\t1. **⚠ `stats --format json` + any breakdown flag emits invalid combined output** (bf-20da,\n179\t   still present). The `--by-type` / `--by-priority` / `--by-assignee` / `--by-label` blocks\n180\t   (`src/cli/mod.rs:2599-2630`) run *after* the format match and always use plain `println!`\n181\t   text regardless of `--format`. So `bf stats --format json --by-type` prints the JSON object\n182\t   **followed by** un-ignorable text (\"By type: …\"). The combined stdout is not valid JSON.\n183\t   **Fix:** when `format == \"json\"`, fold breakdowns into the object as nested maps\n184\t   (`by_type`/`by_priority`/…) instead of printing text.\n185\t\n186\t2. **`show` wraps a single bead in an array** (`:1464`). Intentional and now documented in a\n187\t   code comment: NEEDLE's `parse_single_bead` expects `Vec<Bead>` and takes the first element.\n188\t   Surprising for a user expecting a bare object, but correct for the NEEDLE contract. **Action:\n189\t   surface this in `--help` / README**, not change the behavior.\n190\t\n191\t3. **`ready`'s `[]` empty case diverges from its JSONL siblings.** Minor, but it means\n192\t   `bf ready --format json` on an empty board yields a valid JSON value while `bf list --format\n193\t   json` on an empty board yields an empty string. Either make `list`/`search`/`recent` emit\n194\t   `[]` on empty, or drop `ready`'s special case.\n195\t\n196\t---\n197\t\n198\t## 6. Inconsistencies in array / object formatting\n\nAfter `ready`'s migration, the old headline inconsistency (list/search JSONL vs. ready array)\nis gone. What remains:\n\n1. **Container shape for \"list of beads\" is JSONL, but `show` is a 1-element array, and\n   `ready`'s empty case is `[]`.**\n   - `list`/`search`/`recent`/`ready`(non-empty) → JSONL (no array, no `[…]`)\n   - `ready` (empty) → `[]`\n   - `show` → always `[{…}]` (even though it is logically a single bead)\n   - The remaining list-style commands that *do* use arrays (`velocity`, `log`, `mitosis`,\n     `labels`) emit arrays of non-`Issue` rows, so the JSONL-vs-array split is now strictly\n     \"Issue lists = JSONL, everything else = array.\" That is a defensible rule, but it is\n     **undocumented** and breaks the reasonable expectation that `--format json` yields a\n     parseable JSON document (JSONL is not a single JSON value).\n\n2. **Empty-case handling differs across list-style commands.**\n   - `list`/`search`/`recent` → *no output at all* (empty string). A consumer reading stdout\n     gets `EOF`/parse error, not `[]`.\n   - `ready` → `[]`\n   - `claim` → `{}` (single-object shape; appropriate)\n   - `velocity`/`log`/`mitosis`/`labels` → `[]`\n   - `stats`/`critical-path`/`dep tree` → always emit a full object (never truly \"empty\")\n\n3. **Compact vs. pretty printing.**\n   - Compact (`to_string` / JSONL): `list`, `search`, `recent`, `ready`, `show`, `claim`\n   - Pretty (`to_string_pretty`, 2-space indent): `stats`, `velocity`, `log`, `dep tree`,\n     `labels`, `schema`, `mitosis`, `critical-path`\n   - No command lets the user choose; it is hard-coded per command.\n\n4. **Trailing newline.**\n   - Family A uses `print!` (the only newlines are the JSONL separators; no trailing newline\n     after the last object).\n   - Family B uses `println!` (trailing newline).\n   - A consumer doing `bf search --format json | jq` is fine, but byte-for-byte stable\n     consumers notice.\n\n5. **Key ordering.**\n   - Struct-`Serialize` (`list`/`search`/`recent`/`ready`/`show`, `stats`, `velocity`, `log`,\n     `labels`, `mitosis`, `critical-path`) → **struct declaration order**.\n   - `json!` macro (`claim`, `dep tree`, `schema` `\"all\"`) → **alphabetical**. `serde_json`\n     in `Cargo.toml` does **not** enable `preserve_order`, so `json!` builds a `BTreeMap`-backed\n     `Map` and `Value::Display` sorts keys. (Empirically verified for `claim` in bf-2x0p.)\n   - Harmless to generic-object parsers; differs byte-for-byte.\n\n---\n\n## 5.
